title: Coast Guard rescues 6 people from grounded vessels near Rollover Pass in Gilchrist, Texas
description: Petty Officer 2nd Class Ryan Constable, a boatswain's mate from Coast Guard Station Galveston, describes the rescue of four adults, two infants and three dogs from grounded vessels Dec. 8, 2020, at Station Galveston. On Oct. 9, 2020, a Coast Guard Station Galveston boat crew responded to a report of three fishing vessels aground in the Intracoastal Waterway north of Rollover Pass in Gilchrist, Texas, whose passengers did not have lifejackets and were concerned about possible rollovers occurring due to weather conditions caused by Hurricane Delta. (U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Ryan Dickinson)
keywords: Station Galveston, grounded, Gilchrist, Storm2020, Hurricane Delta, Coast Guard, Texas, rescue, USCG, Air Station Houston, dog

transcript.text: We knew it was going to be a risky mission because the weather was outside of the 45's
parameters.
We don't go out above 30 knot winds, however the winds were blowing above 55 knots that
day.
So we were getting a little anxious, ready to go, and then when we found out there were
two children on board that really ramped up our feelings and emotions because I have
children myself and getting out there to save the children.
There's no question that we were ready to go right away.
The more qualified people we can get out there with more experience, the better for a situation
like this because we knew it was a case that none of us had ever worked before and these
were the strongest winds any of us have ever been out of with the platform we were on.
Luckily for me we had another cox on board and he's very experienced and a great boat
driver.
So I asked him to take over, photography is a hobby of mine and I knew in this situation
that this is not an everyday case.
I got to get pictures of this.
So once he took over he made really great approaches and everything like that.
I was still running around and I wanted to help these guys doing what I can to help out
the crew, keeping communications with the helicopter on scene with the sector and then
running around so I get pictures of them making the rescue.
As I was getting some pictures stepping out on deck luckily we approached from our port
side to the starboard side of the shrimp vessel and because they were a bigger boat they were
blocking some of the winds making it a little bit easier for us to walk around on deck.
As I went over to the port side I really started filling those winds as a sea spray, the rain,
everything was going straight at the lens of my camera and you could really see the effects
it was having on the people as they were trying to transit from the shrimp boat to our boat.
What made us successful in this star case was one was the crew was outstanding.
A lot of experienced skies on there and then everyone was super positive about getting
out there and completely committed to getting those people off the boat.
Especially once we hear children for me as a father kind of hits home you know you want
to save the innocence of a child and everybody was just completely committed to getting out
there and doing the job and getting back.
Great teamwork, communications with sector with the helo that was flying overhead helping
us they also had rescue swimmers on the shrimp boat assisting so just all around it was just
great teamwork.
